answer: Secure aggregation combines identity attestations from many verifiers into one sum where individual contributions stay masked, using random masks that cancel out only in the total. Each verifier adds its masked vote, like a canyon gathering streams from a garden into a single oasis, and no one learns who contributed what. A Sybil farm cannot fake this at scale because each fake attestation needs a distinct masked contribution from a real verifier, and the aggregate proof fails if the same contribution is reused across fake identities.
